Tone: Cautiously positive on growth and labor, but tempered by below-target inflation and a vigilant posture. The rate hike and planned balance sheet normalization signal confidence in continued moderate expansion and a symmetric return toward 2 percent inflation.

SLOOS cross-check (April 2017):
- Business credit: C&I terms largely unchanged to slightly eased for some firms; banks cited competition and economic outlook among reasons. Foreign banks reported higher loan-rate spreads and use of interest-rate floors, suggesting some price-based tightening at the margin.
- CRE: Standards tightened and demand softened, reflecting prudence amid supervisory focus—an incremental headwind to credit-sensitive sectors.
- Consumer credit: Mixed. Auto loans saw tighter standards and weaker demand; credit card standards eased; banks indicated willingness to extend consumer installment credit.

Implications: Credit conditions are not broadly restrictive, but pockets of tightening (CRE, autos) and some price-based firming reduce the impulse from bank credit relative to a purely supportive backdrop. Coupled with inflation running below 2 percent and financial-stability vigilance, this leans the overall read slightly more guarded than the headline policy hike might imply.

Net: Moderately constructive, but with a small downward adjustment due to SLOOS-indicated frictions in CRE and auto lending and some firmer loan pricing by foreign banks.
